facts.text: Bahena is a member of the 10th District Council, which covers North and South Lawndale, Little Village and a portion of Pilsen, and serves as its Nominating Committee member.

priorities.text: Says she has worked on the council for community-centered public safety, accountability and stronger protections for immigrant families.

facts.text: David Orlikoff is a member of the 14th Police District Council; he assumed office on May 2, 2023, and his current term ends on May 4, 2027.
He received the most votes in the 14th District’s 2023 council race, 16,483.
In a 2023 Chicago Reader candidate questionnaire he selected options such as defunding police and increasing civilian oversight of the department.
In December 2024, 19 district council members from 13 police districts signed a letter asking him to resign; he did not resign.
A September 2024 measure at a citywide district council meeting asking the CCPSA to censure him failed by one vote.
In 2024 Ald. Scott Waguespack filed a complaint with the Office of Inspector General alleging Orlikoff violated the City’s workplace violence policy; the OIG declined to comment on it.
At least three City Council members have asked the Inspector General and the Chicago Board of Ethics to investigate his conduct.
In August 2026 he and Ashley Vargas voted to censure chair Christopher Laurent, and Orlikoff became the council’s nominating committee member.

priorities.text: Proposed a policy brief, adopted by the council, calling on the CCPSA to end pretextual traffic stops for low-level violations and suspicionless consent searches.
Calls for removing Chicago police officers with ties to extremist groups such as the Oath Keepers and Proud Boys.
Opposed an increase in the Chicago Police Department budget.
At a May 2026 council meeting he summarized the CARE alternative crisis response pilot expansion, citing needs for more funding, 911 training and clearer police–CARE routing.
Has called for the State’s Attorney to investigate federal immigration agent misconduct and killings.
Introduced council bylaws stating that groups not empowered by the bylaws should not imply they represent the council.
